summary: The study reports the low-temperature, selective atomic layer deposition (ALD) of nickel metal thin films using bis(1,4-di-tert-butyl-1,3-diazadienyl)nickel and tert-butylamine as precursors. The process demonstrates self-limited growth with a growth rate of 0.60 Å/cycle within an ALD window of 180 to 195 °C. Nickel metal films were grown on metal substrates such as platinum and ruthenium, showing low surface roughness and high purity. The process inherently selects for metal substrates over insulators.
evidence: We report the growth of nickel metal films by atomic layer deposition (ALD) employing bis(1,4-di-tert-butyl-1,3-diazadienyl)nickel and tert-butylamine as the precursors. ... The nickel metal ALD process was further explored at 180 °C on platinum substrates by growing films with differing numbers of cycles. ... Nickel metal films were grown on platinum substrates at 180 °C with 300 (18 nm thick) and 1000 (60 nm thick) cycles. ... Nickel metal ALD occurs with inherent selectivity on metal surfaces under all conditions that were explored.
